extracted.intended_audience: contributors to mathlib / Lean developers writing mathlib code
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of mathlib's style linters: a set of stylistic checks (warnings) for Lean/mathlib source code, describing what patterns are disallowed or discouraged and configuration defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style linters (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: This file contains linters about stylistic aspects: these are only about coding style, but do not affect correctness nor global coherence of mathlib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All of these linters are enabled in mathlib by default, but disabled globally since they enforce conventions which are inherently subjective. Historically some were ported from the lint-style.py Python script.

rubrics_metrics.name: setOption linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The setOption linter emits a warning on a set_option command, term or tactic which sets a pp, profiler or trace option. It also warns on an option containing maxHeartbeats (as these should be scoped as set_option ... in a single command instead).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disallowed options are those meant to be temporary and not for polished code. The linter detects set_option occurrences (isSetOption). Avoid global or file-scoped use of pp/profiler/trace settings and unscoped maxHeartbeats; prefer scoping such options to single commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: missingEnd linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The missingEnd linter emits a warning on non-closed sections and namespaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It allows the 'outermost' noncomputable section to be left open (whether or not it is named). Closing all sections/namespaces helps when minimising files or moving code between files.

rubrics_metrics.name: cdot linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The cdot linter flags uses of the 'cdot' · that are achieved by typing a character different from ·. For instance, a plain dot '.' is allowed syntax, but is flagged by the linter. It also flags 'isolated cdots' i.e. when the · is on its own line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathlib prefers uniform use of the actual cdot character rather than typing a plain '.' to achieve the same effect. The linter provides helpers (isCDot?) to detect such cases. Avoid isolated cdot lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: dollarSyntax linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The dollarSyntax linter flags uses of the <| pipe that are achieved by typing $.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are disallowed by the mathlib style guide because using <| pairs better with |> for symmetry. Use the explicit <| token rather than $.

rubrics_metrics.name: lambdaSyntax linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The lambdaSyntax linter flags uses of the symbol λ to define anonymous functions, as opposed to the fun keyword. These are syntactically equivalent; mathlib style prefers the latter as it is considered more readable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'fun' over 'λ' for anonymous functions to improve readability. The linter can extract Term.fun nodes to find occurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: longFile linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The longFile linter emits a warning on files which are longer than a certain number of lines (1500 by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configuration: linter.style.longFileDefValue determines the default line limit used by mathlib. If set to N lines, the linter warns once a file has more than N lines. A value of 0 silences the linter entirely. Long files are discouraged; split very large files.

rubrics_metrics.name: longLine linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The longLine linter emits a warning on lines longer than linter.style.longLine.maxLineLength (which defaults to 100) characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configuration option longLine.maxLineLength controls the maximum allowed length. Lines containing URLs are allowed to be longer. Keep most lines under the configured maximum (default 100).

rubrics_metrics.name: nameCheck linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The nameCheck linter emits a warning on declarations whose name is non-standard style. (Currently, this only includes declarations whose name includes a double underscore.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Why is this bad? Double underscores in theorem names can be considered non-standard and probably were introduced by accident. How to fix this? Use single underscores to separate parts of a name, following standard naming conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: openClassical linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The openClassical linter emits a warning on open Classical statements which are not scoped to a single declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-scoped open Classical can hide that some theorem statements would be better stated with explicit decidability statements. The linter only checks independent open commands; open ... in ... commands are not flagged by this check. Helpers exist to extract opened names (extractOpenNames). Prefer scoping open Classical to single declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: show linter
rubrics_metrics.description: The show linter emits a warning if the show tactic changed the goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: show should only be used to indicate intermediate goal states for proof readability. When the goal is actually changed, prefer using change instead.
